scheme_name: Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development
description:
The Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This initiative aims to conserve and promote indigenous breeds of cattle, particularly focusing on the Murrah breed of buffaloes. 

The Murrah buffalo is renowned for its high milk yield and adaptability to various climatic conditions. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the population of indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds. 

The government aims to increase the population of indigenous cattle by 20 percent by the year 2025. 

Additionally, the scheme seeks to improve the genetic quality of these breeds through selective breeding programs. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the productivity of indigenous cattle by providing better nutrition and healthcare. 

Financial assistance is provided under this scheme to farmers for the purchase of indigenous cattle. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 30,000 for purchasing a Murrah buffalo under this scheme. 

The scheme also includes provisions for establishing breeding centers for indigenous cattle. 

These breeding centers are aimed at improving the genetic quality of the cattle. 

The government allocates funds for the establishment of these centers, which are expected to be operational by 2025. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of training farmers in modern cattle management practices. 

Training programs are conducted to educate farmers about the benefits of indigenous breeds. 

The government aims to train at least 50,000 farmers under this scheme by the end of 2025. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on farmers engaged in dairy farming. 

Farmers must own a minimum of two acres of agricultural land to qualify for the benefits. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for eligibility. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must first visit the nearest Animal Husbandry Department office. 

They need to fill out an application form available at the office. 

Farmers must provide documents such as proof of land ownership and identity proof. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the officials. 

After verification, eligible farmers are notified about the financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done within 30 days of approval. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

Contact details for the Department can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote sustainable agriculture and rural development. 

It aligns with the National Livestock Policy, which emphasizes the conservation of indigenous breeds. 

The government has allocated INR 200 crores for the implementation of this scheme. 

This funding is aimed at supporting various activities under the scheme, including breeding programs and farmer training. 

The scheme also encourages the establishment of cooperatives among farmers. 

These cooperatives can help in collective purchasing and marketing of indigenous cattle. 

The government aims to establish at least 1,000 cooperatives by 2025. 

The scheme has a significant focus on research and development. 

Research institutions are encouraged to study the genetic traits of indigenous breeds. 

This research is aimed at improving breeding techniques and cattle management practices. 

The government also promotes the use of artificial insemination to enhance genetic diversity. 

Artificial insemination centers are being set up across various states. 

These centers will facilitate the breeding of high-quality indigenous cattle. 

The scheme also addresses the nutritional needs of indigenous cattle. 

Farmers are provided with guidelines on proper feeding and care. 

The government promotes the use of locally available feed resources. 

This initiative aims to reduce the cost of cattle rearing for farmers. 

The scheme also includes provisions for veterinary care. 

Farmers are encouraged to vaccinate their cattle against common diseases. 

The government provides financial assistance for veterinary services. 

This assistance can cover up to 50 percent of the costs incurred by farmers. 

The scheme has been well-received by the farming community. 

Many farmers have reported increased milk production after adopting indigenous breeds. 

The government conducts regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme. 

This evaluation helps in assessing the impact of the scheme on farmers' livelihoods. 

The scheme also aims to promote the cultural significance of indigenous breeds. 

Indigenous cattle are an integral part of rural life and traditions in India. 

The government encourages the participation of women in dairy farming under this scheme. 

Women farmers are provided with additional training and support. 

The scheme aims to empower women by promoting their involvement in livestock management. 

The government also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in cattle rearing. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt organic farming practices in conjunction with cattle rearing. 

This approach aims to enhance the overall productivity of the farm. 

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the rural economy. 

By promoting indigenous breeds, the government aims to reduce dependency on exotic breeds. 

This will help in conserving the genetic diversity of livestock in India. 

The scheme also aligns with global efforts to promote biodiversity. 

The government is committed to ensuring the long-term sustainability of indigenous cattle breeds. 

This commitment is reflected in the comprehensive approach of the scheme. 

The Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development is a vital initiative for rural development. 

It aims to improve the livelihoods of farmers while conserving valuable genetic resources. 

The success of this scheme will depend on the active participation of farmers and local communities. 

The government continues to seek feedback from stakeholders to improve the implementation of the scheme. 

Overall, this initiative represents a significant step towards promoting indigenous cattle in India. 

It aims to create a sustainable and productive dairy sector that benefits farmers and the environment.
